items.readme:
rust-anything

Rewrite your whole app in Rust. Keep it working the whole way.

CLIs, servers and libraries, piece by piece, checked against the original at every step.

up to 20x faster · 38,251 recorded cases replayed · 0 mismatches · one command

**Rewrite your whole app in Rust, one piece at a time.** rust-anything records what your TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, C, Go, Ruby or Java app does today, then checks every piece of the Rust rewrite against that recording before it moves on, until the app is pure Rust. CLIs, HTTP servers and libraries; your coding agent (or you) writes the Rust. It can only catch what the recording covers: see [What it can't catch](#what-it-cant-catch). Only need the slow part fast? Port just that, one hot path at a time: | Real workload, same results as the original | Original | With rust-anything | | --- | ---: | ---: | | x18n's sidebar search, 50,000 keys (TypeScript, Node) | 10 ms per query | **0.5 ms: 20x faster** | | The same search in the browser (wasm, one thread) | 10 ms | **0.95 ms: 11.5x** | | `slugify` over 20,000 strings (Python) | 98 ms | **17x faster** | | `Shellwords.shellescape` from Ruby's standard library, 50,000 values | 88 ms | **11.8x faster** | | `Slugify` over 50,000 strings (Go) | 49 ms | **4x faster** | | `slugify` over 50,000 strings (Java) | 43 ms | **3x faster** |

Measured on 4 cores; every number has a benchmark in [`demo/`](./demo) that first checks the results are identical. Calling Rust once per small function is usually *slower* than a JIT; rust-anything finds the loop worth moving, and moves it. > rust-anything is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by the Rust Project > or the Rust Foundation. "Rust" is a trademark of the Rust Foundation. ## Quick start Paste this into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Gemini CLI and let your agent install it: ```text Install rust-anything: run `cargo install rust-anything`, then `rust-anything setup`. Tell me when to restart you. ``` Or yourself: ```sh cargo install rust-anything # from crates.io rust-anything setup # registers it with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI ``` No Rust toolchain yet? Prebuilt binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows are attached to each [GitHub release](https://github.com/erkamyaman/rust-anything/releases), and for JavaScript projects `npm install -g rust-anything` installs the same binary. In Claude Code you can also install it as a plugin (the MCP server and the skill; the CLI above must be on your `PATH`): ```text /plugin install rust-anything --marketplace erkamyaman/rust-anything ``` `setup` adds the MCP server to each agent it finds and installs the workflow skill where the agent reads skills. It keeps your other settings, is safe to run again, and `--remove` undoes it. Then ask your agent, for example: - *"Rewrite this CLI in Rust with rust-anything, end to end, and prove it behaves the same."* - *"This search feels slow. Profile it with rust-anything and move the hot loop to Rust."* - *"Plan a migration of `src/parser/` to Rust with rust-anything; port the first unit and prove it."* - *"Bench the Rust port in `rust/text-rs` against the original and tell me whether to ship it."* ### Works with | Agent | `rust-anything setup` adds | | --- | --- | | Claude Code | MCP server in `~/.claude.json`, skill in `~/.claude/skills/` | | Codex | MCP server in `~/.codex/config.toml`, skill in `~/.codex/skills/` | | Cursor | MCP server in `~/.cursor/mcp.json` | | Gemini CLI | MCP server in `~/.gemini/settings.json` | | Any other MCP client | add `rust-anything mcp` as a stdio server by hand (see [Install](#install)) | Before changing a file that exists, `setup` saves a copy beside it (`.rust-anything.bak`). Or run the steps yourself:

```sh rust-anything profile . -- node bench.mjs # what is hot, and who calls it rust-anything bridge . src/fuzzy.ts --batch fuzzyScore:text # write src/port.rs (or let your agent), then: rust-anything record rust/fuzzy-rs && rust-anything build rust/fuzzy-rs rust-anything diff rust/fuzzy-rs # every recorded case must match rust-anything bench rust/fuzzy-rs # faster? the verdict says rust-anything gate rust/fuzzy-rs # done means this passes ``` rust-anything does not translate code: your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ...) or you write the Rust. rust-anything supplies what an agent cannot guess reliably: where the time goes, what to port first and in which order, a bridge so the rest of the code calls the Rust with its API unchanged, the exact behavior the port must match, a safe way to ship it, and a gate that says when a port is done. ## Languages | Language | Unit | Bridge | Recorded and replayed by | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | TypeScript/JavaScript | folder or file | napi-rs or wasm-bindgen with a generated binary wire; classes and async included | Node, running the `.ts` sources | | Python | package or module | PyO3 (abi3), direct conversion, typed exceptions | Python, importing the original | | C | `.c` file | `extern "C"` functions with the original names and a header | the original compiled to a shared library, called through ctypes, one fork per case | | Go | package | typed cgo calls and a generated binary wire, in a package with the original API | a generated Go driver, built as its own module | | Ruby | file or folder of module functions | a magnus extension under the original modules | a generated Ruby driver | | Java | package of `public static` methods | typed JNI and a generated binary wire, in wrapper classes with the original methods | a generated reflection driver | | PHP (preview) | folder of functions and `public static` methods | coming next: PHP FFI over a C ABI | whole apps today: `app record`, `app replay` and the front door, for CLIs and servers (`php -S`) | | C# (preview) | folder of `public static` methods | coming next: P/Invoke over a C ABI | whole apps today: `app record`, `app replay` and the front door, for CLIs and ASP.NET servers (`dotnet .dll`) | Every language except C also gets batch classes (`--batch`): the items cross once and stay in Rust, and each call runs over all of them on all cores. The language is detected from the repository (`go.mod`, `pom.xml`, a `.csproj` or `.sln`, `pyproject.toml`, `Gemfile`, `composer.json`, `package.json`, else the most common source files); `--lang` overrides it. Types come from the source: TS types, Python hints, C, Go, Java and C# signatures, Ruby YARD tags, PHP types and phpdoc; untyped parameters used as numbers are inferred as numbers. PHP is in preview: `analyze` plans a PHP app (Composer packages and PSR-4 autoloading, risks such as loose comparison and integer overflow into floats, Composer packages mapped to crates), and a PHP CLI or server can be recorded, replayed and put behind a Rust front door. Porting its units into Rust through PHP's FFI is the next step ([issue #2](https://github.com/erkamyaman/rust-anything/issues/2)). C# is in preview the same way: `analyze` reads `.csproj` projects and their NuGet packages (mapped to crates), resolves `using` directives to folders, and flags what C# does differently (`decimal`, `dynamic`, LINQ's deferred queries, `Task`, `lock`, reflection). A C# CLI or ASP.NET server can be recorded, replayed and put behind a Rust front door; porting units through P/Invoke comes next. ## How it works ``` profile ──> analyze ──> bridge ──> record ──> port.rs ──> diff ──> bench ──> shadow ──> gate where the what to the Rust what the you or every faster? both side done means time goes port first crate and original your agent recorded the by side in this passes wrapper does write it case verdict production ``` The original stays the source of truth: `record` runs it on edge cases (and your own inputs) and saves what it returns or throws; `diff` replays every case against the Rust; nothing ships until they all match and `gate` passes. Callers keep the original API throughout. A whole app goes through the same loop unit by unit, inside a frame that proves the whole program ([Port a whole app](#port-a-whole-app)): ``` analyze --whole-app ──> app record ──> app front-door ──> per unit: the loop above, then app wire ──> app lift shape, every what the app Rust owns the gate passes, so the unit answers in pure Rust, dependency, the does from the entry point; the Rust: replay 100%, fallback rate down proved by decisions to make outside original answers replay ``` ## The loop | Step | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | 0. Profile | `rust-anything profile -- node bench.mjs` | Runs a real workload under the language's profiler (node, cProfile, `go test` pprof, JFR, a Ruby tracer): hot functions by inclusive time, their callers, and which loops to batch; flags code that is already compiled (numba, Cython, JAX), where Rust gains little | | 1. Plan | `rust-anything analyze ` | Units, port order, risks with `file:line`, bridge per unit, dependency-to-crate fit, best first ports; `--whole-app` adds entry points and shape, every dependency (imported or declared) with its crate, pieces (units that import each other move together) and numbered decisions with a recommended answer | | 2. Bridge | `rust-anything bridge ` | Crate with the bindings (`lib.rs`, plus the wrapper the source language loads) and stubs to port (`port.rs`); `--batch fn:param` adds a class that keeps many `param` values in Rust | | 3. Record | `rust-anything record ` | Runs the original on generated edge cases (non-ASCII, emoji, `-0`, `NaN`, ints where floats are expected, ...) and on every semantic trap in every parameter (string length and case, signed division, overflow edges, float printing, map and sort order), and saves `cases.jsonl`; `--float-tolerance 1e-9` lets floats match within that share for numeric code | | 3. Build | `rust-anything build ` | Builds the Rust side: `.node`, wasm package, Python extension or shared library | | 3. Diff | `rust-anything diff ` | Replays the recorded cases against Rust, called the way the original's callers call it; lists mismatches | | 3. Bench | `rust-anything bench ` | Times the recorded cases on the original and on Rust, bridge included | | 4. Shadow | `rust-anything shadow ` | Drop-in that runs both, returns the original's result, reports mismatches; `RUST_ANYTHING_MODE=old\|shadow\|new` | | 5. Gate | `rust-anything gate ` | fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, tests, `unsafe` audit, nothing unported, a recorded failing case for every error path of the original, no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` where the original returns an error (unless marked `// INFALLIBLE: `), build, API, behavior | | Agents | `rust-anything setup` | Registers the MCP server (`rust-anything mcp`, every step as a tool) and the workflow skill ([`skills/rust-anything/SKILL.md`](./skills/rust-anything/SKILL.md)) with your coding agents | ## Port a whole app The goal is a pure Rust app that behaves like the original, with the original kept as reference. Your agent writes the Rust; rust-anything orders the work, scaffolds it, and proves every step. The [whole-app skill](./skills/rust-anything/whole-app.md) walks the agent through it, starting with the decisions only you can make: - **Grilling**: the agent asks in rounds, each question with its recommended answer, until every decision the port depends on is settled, and writes each one as an ADR in `rust/DECISIONS.md`, with `rust/GLOSSARY.md` mapping the original's terms to Rust names. - **Research**: background agents read each dependency's primary sources and write `rust/research/.md`, with every semantic trap they found. - **Across sessions**: `rust/MAP.md` lists every unit with its state; a session claims one unit before it starts, and each checkpoint leaves a `rust/HANDOFF.md` for the next session. Units in one wave can be ported in parallel by subagents. - **Cutover**: the agent does what it can and writes `rust/cutover.sh`, an interactive script for the steps only you can do (deploys, DNS, secrets), with a way back at each step. Grilling, research and these practices are adapted from [Matt Pocock's skills](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills). Plan first: `rust-anything analyze . --whole-app` adds the app's shape (CLI, server or library) and entry points, every external dependency (imported or declared) with its Rust crate and fit, the port order as pieces (units that import each other move together), and numbered decisions with a recommended answer: keep units, blocked units, dependencies with no or a partial crate. Then prove the whole program from the outside. `record` and `diff` prove one unit; `app record` and `app replay` prove the app, for CLIs and servers in any of the six languages (the app is a black box): ```sh rust-anything app record . -- python3 cli.py # the command that runs the original rust-anything app replay . # the original must pass 100% rust-anything app replay . --build "target/release/mytool" ``` - `app record` runs the original on the app's own documented examples (`$ mytool ...` lines in its Markdown and shell files, with the files they name), an `--inputs` JSONL file (`{"name", "args", "stdin", "env", "files"}`), and semantic traps derived from those cases (non-ASCII and emoji strings, negative division and modulo, overflow, large and tiny floats, map order, missing files). Each case runs twice; what differs between the two runs becomes a `[..]` wildcard. `--normalize timestamps|uuids|key-order` or `--normalize name=regex` adds normalizers, saved with the cases. - Cases are [trycmd](https://docs.rs/trycmd) files in `rust/app-cases/`: `.toml` (argv, env, exit code), `.stdin`, `.stdout`, `.stderr`, `.in/` (files in) and `.out/` (files written). Read and edit them by hand; a Rust test can run them with `trycmd` once the port has a binary. - `app replay` runs any build against the cases, prints `passed/total`, writes `rust/app-cases/replay-report.md` with a diff per failing case, and exits non-zero on any mismatch. A build that appends to the file named by `RUST_ANYTHING_FALLBACK_LOG` (one line per fallback to the original), as the front door below does, also gets its fallback rate reported. - `app replay --case ` reruns one case by the name the report gives it: the fast, repeatable loop for fixing a mismatch before running everything again. Then move the entry point to Rust and hand it commands one unit at a time: ```sh rust-anything app front-door . # rust/app: every command runs the original rust-anything app wire . textkit --command upper # after textkit-rs passes gate # write the glue in rust/app/src/units/textkit.rs, then: rust-anything app wire . textkit # 100% again, lower fallback rate ``` - `app front-door` scaffolds `rust/app`, a Rust binary named after the app: a clap parser for the commands and flags in the recorded cases, where every command runs the original with the same argv, stdin and environment and passes its output and exit code through. Each fallback is counted, so replaying the fresh front door gives 100% passed at 100% fallback (it builds and replays to show it). It never overwrites `rust/app`: the code is yours from then on. - `app wire --command ` runs `gate` on the unit crate (`--skip-gate` if it just passed), adds it to `rust/app` as a library, writes `src/units/.rs` once for you or your agent to fill in (parse the arguments, call `::port`, print what the original prints), routes the commands to it, then builds and replays. `RUST_ANYTHING_UNIT_=original` sends a wired unit back to the original until the lift. Wire the app's own name as a command (`--command mytool`) for argv that names no command: no arguments, unknown commands, usage errors. When replay passes with fallback rate 0 and every unit passes gate, make it a pure Rust app: ```sh rust-anything app lift . ``` - `app lift` refuses until both hold, and says what blocks it: the cases still falling back, glue still a stub, units failing gate. - On a copy first, it removes the fallback path and the kill switches, turns each unit crate into a plain library of `rust/app` (no `cdylib`, bindings or generated wrappers), and adds `rust/app/tests/app_cases.rs`, which runs `rust/app-cases` with trycmd on `cargo test`, so CI needs nothing but cargo. - Then it runs the lift checklist: fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and tests on every unit and on `rust/app`, every target named in `rust/DECISIONS.md` built or checked where it is installed, files read at run time and asset folders not embedded, and replay on the pure binary. Only when all of it passes are the changes written back. The original is never touched. ### Servers The same commands prove HTTP servers. `--http` says the command starts a server; it takes its port from `PORT` or `{port}` in the command (`--port` for one that always listens on the same port): ```sh rust-anything app record . --http -- node server.js rust-anything app replay . rust-anything app front-door . # axum: every route proxied rust-anything app wire . api --route 'GET /users/{id}' --route '*' rust-anything app lift . ``` - Requests come from `curl` lines in the app's docs (`curl -X POST -d ... http://localhost:8080/x`), `--inputs` (`{"name", "method", "path", "headers", "body"}`) and traps: path segments and query values swapped for the same traps as CLI arguments, bodies for text and JSON traps, and an unknown route. Each run starts the server fresh and sends the requests in name order, so state between requests is kept. - Cases are `rust/app-cases/http/.toml` (the request, the status and the headers that matter) and `.body` (the response body, with `[..]` where two runs differed). Date, server and other per-response headers are left out; delete any header line you do not care about. - The front door is an axum server that starts the original on a port of its own and proxies every route no unit answers. `wire --route` takes axum routes: `METHOD /path/{param}`, `/path` for any method, `*` for everything else; the glue gets the route, its parameters and the request. `lift` removes the proxy; HTTP cases then run in CI with `app replay`. ### Libraries A library has no process to replay: its public API is the front door, and each unit's recorded cases are the proof. ```sh rust-anything app front-door . # rust/app: a Rust crate with the public API # each unit through the loop: bridge, record, port.rs, build, diff, gate; then: rust-anything app wire . textkit-rs # re-exported from rust/app; the original imports its shadow rust-anything app replay . # every wired unit's cases; fallback = exports still in the original rust-anything app lift . ``` - `app front-door` finds the public API (every unit's exports) when the repository has no `main` and no server (`--library` otherwise), and scaffolds `rust/app` as a library crate. Each wired unit becomes a module of it: `pub use textkit_rs::port as textkit;`. - `app wire` takes a crate made by `bridge`, runs `gate`, and writes the unit's shadow drop-in: the original package imports it in place of the unit, so its callers keep the original API and reach the Rust. `RUST_ANYTHING_UNIT_=original` sends the unit back (C: build without the shadow's flags). - `app replay` runs every wired unit's recorded cases through its bindings. The fallback rate is the share of public exports Rust does not answer yet: unwired units, and exports `bridge` keeps in the original language. - `app lift` needs fallback 0 and every unit through `gate`; it strips the bindings, wrappers and shadows from the units and leaves `rust/app` as one pure Rust library. It does not touch any `port.rs`, so the cases that matched through the bindings still describe it; the checklist warns about files of the original that still import the shadows. All five are MCP tools too: `app_record`, `app_replay`, `app_front_door`, `app_wire` and `app_lift`. ## Case study: x18n's core All 29 functions of x18n's core that can move without an API change were ported with rust-anything: every gate passes and 7,925 recorded cases match exactly. `rust-anything bench` then showed the ports are slower than the TS as called from JS, because the bridge costs more than the work. Full report: [`demo/x18n-core`](./demo/x18n-core/README.md). The lesson is built in: measure with `bench` before shipping a port. ## Hot paths: keep the data in Rust A port called once per item pays the bridge once per item, and loses to a JIT. What wins is moving the loop: `profile` finds it, and `--batch` generates a class that takes the items once and runs the function over all of them per call, on all cores, with typed-array results. ```sh rust-anything profile ../x18n -- node --experimental-strip-types $PWD/demo/x18n-search/search.ts . # -> fuzzyScore: a quarter of the run, called per key by `matched`: batch it rust-anything bridge ../x18n packages/core/src/fuzzy.ts --batch fuzzyScore:text ``` ```js const search = new FuzzyScoreBatch(keys) // once const order = search.rank(query, 0) // per keystroke: indexes, best first ``` A `FuzzyScoreIndex` struct in `port.rs` replaces the default loop with one that prepares the items once, and can rank by itself (`rank`): it keeps the keys lowercased with a character mask each, a table of each key's first position of every common character (a one-letter query is one column), and the last query's matches (typing `se` after `s` rescores only what `s` matched). On x18n's sidebar search over 50,000 keys, typed letter by letter, with identical results: | | Per query | vs TS | | --- | ---: | ---: | | TS: `map(fuzzyScore)`, filter, sort | 10 ms | 1x | | TS with the same narrowing as the index | 4.1-5.4 ms | 2x | | The same port, called per key | - | 0.2-0.4x | | `FuzzyScoreBatch`, default index (4 cores) | 5.1 ms | 1.7x | | `FuzzyScoreBatch` with `FuzzyScoreIndex` (napi, 4 cores) | 0.45-0.56 ms | **18-22x** | | The same with wasm (one thread) | 0.95 ms | **11.5x** | Against TS doing the same narrowing, Rust is still 7-12x faster (wasm 5x). Turn the returned indexes into keys with a plain loop: `Array.from(order, i => keys[i])` cost 20x more, 0.4 ms. Every language gets batches, and they beat the original even where per-call ports lose. The same work on 4 cores, identical results and errors (benchmarks in each demo folder): | Language | Workload | Original | Per-call port vs original | Batch vs original | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | TS | x18n search, 50,000 keys | 10 ms | 0.2-0.4x | **20x** | | Python | `slugify`, 20,000 strings | 98 ms | - | **17x** | | Ruby | `slugify`, 20,000 strings | 110 ms | - | **12.7x** | | Ruby | `shellescape` (stdlib), 50,000 mixed values | 88 ms | - | **11.8x** | | Go | `Slugify`, 50,000 strings | 49 ms | 0.93x | **4x** | | Java | `slugify`, 50,000 strings | 43 ms | 0.68x | **3x** | Compiled originals gain less: the per-item work is already fast, so the batch wins by the number of cores. Batch crates allocate with mimalloc: with the system allocator the Go batch was slower than one thread. Demo: [`demo/x18n-search`](./demo/x18n-search/README.md). ## Real code in six languages Go's `path`, Ruby's `shellwords`, Python's `colorsys`, JDK and glibc behavior behind small facades: every port passes its gate, 13,010 recorded cases in all. The runs found and fixed bugs in rust-anything (floats off by one ULP through `serde_json`, C crashes during recording, untyped code getting garbage inputs). Called per function, the Ruby port runs 4.4x faster than Ruby and the Python port 1.35x faster than CPython, while Go and Java leaf functions stay faster in their own language; as batches, all of them win (see the table above). Report: [`docs/real-world-languages.md`](./docs/real-world-languages.md). ## Example: a real module from x18n `packages/core/src/fuzzy.ts` from [x18n](https://github.com/x18n-dev/x18n), ported both ways in [`demo/`](./demo): ```sh rust-anything analyze ../x18n # fuzzy.ts: ready, wasm-bindgen (core runs in browsers) rust-anything bridge ../x18n packages/core/src/fuzzy.ts --out demo/fuzzy-rs rust-anything record demo/fuzzy-rs --count 2000 # write src/port.rs rust-anything gate demo/fuzzy-rs ``` A first port that indexed by Rust `char` passed simple tests but failed `diff`: ``` 198/200 cases match - fuzzyScore("b😀", "a😀b😀c"): expected {"ok":1997}, got {"ok":1998} ``` JS `indexOf` counts UTF-16 code units, so an emoji is two positions. The port in `demo/*/src/port.rs` uses the generated `utf16` helpers and passes 2000/2000 cases and the gate, as napi-rs (`demo/fuzzy-napi`) and as wasm-bindgen (`demo/fuzzy-rs`). The plan rust-anything writes for all of x18n: [`docs/examples/x18n.md`](./docs/examples/x18n.md). ## Install ```sh cargo install --path . ``` `record`, `diff` and `bench` run the original in its own runtime: Node 22.6+ for TS (it runs `.ts` sources directly), Python 3.9+ for Python and C (ctypes), Go 1.21+, Ruby 3+, JDK 17+ (`javac` and `java`). C also needs a C compiler. wasm bridges also need `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `cargo install wasm-bindgen-cli --version --locked`; `build` names the exact version. For agents, `rust-anything setup` registers everything (see Quick start). To add the MCP server to one project by hand instead (`.mcp.json`): ```json { "mcpServers": { "rust-anything": { "command": "rust-anything", "args": ["mcp"] } } } ``` ## What `bridge` decides - Exports that cannot cross a bridge stay in the source language, with the reason, and the shadow module re-exports the original. For TS: functions that take or return functions, generators and iterators, RegExp, `instanceof` checks, generics, and values whose types (followed through imports, re-exports and `extends`) hold functions. `--keep "name: reason"` keeps more, e.g. code that depends on `Intl` data. - TS types map to Rust types, with type aliases resolved through imports and parameter types inferred from default values; structured values cross as a generated binary wire (JSON only as a fallback for shapes the wire does not model). - JSON cannot express `undefined`, NaN, Infinity, -0 or lone surrogates: structured values carry markers (`{"$undefined": true}`, `{"$num": "NaN"}`, `{"$utf16": [...]}`) that the generated `index.cjs` translates, with helpers in the crate's `js.rs`. `record` runs TS sources as they are: a Node resolve hook follows bundler-style imports (`./errors` to `./errors.ts`), `--resolve-from` supplies npm packages when the repo has none installed, and TS that needs transforming (enums, parameter properties) is retried with `--experimental-transform-types`. ## What `analyze` looks at - Packages (`package.json`) and source files; skips `node_modules`, build output, fixtures, playgrounds, tool configs. Mika

简体中文 · [English](README.en.md) **你手机上的私人 AI 助理，替你操作 App、上网、把事办成。**
它在一块看不见的后台屏上干活，你照样刷你的手机。

⬇ 下载 Mika（安卓 APK）

[安装](#安装) · [快速开始](#快速开始) · [能做什么](#能做什么) · [常见问题](#常见问题) · [参与贡献](#参与贡献)
## 安装 **方式一：在手机上自己装** 1. 从 [Releases](https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/releases/latest) 下载最新的 APK，安装。 2. 打开 Mika 设置里的「设置手机操作」向导，配对一次无线调试（[设置指南](docs/setup-guide.md)）。 3. 在设置里的「模型」添加服务商、填 API Key，或者用 ChatGPT、xAI、OpenRouter 账号登录。 每一步的细节见下文的[快速开始](#快速开始)。 **方式二：让电脑上的 AI 助手帮你装** 手机用数据线连上电脑，在手机上打开 USB 调试（开发者选项里别的开关不要动，除非 AI 助手请你打开；有的会清除手机数据），然后把下面这句话发给电脑上能执行命令的 AI 助手： ``` 请按 https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/blob/main/docs/install-with-agent.md 的步骤，帮我把 Mika 安装到通过 USB 连着的安卓手机上。 ``` 它会检查手机、下载安装、打开需要的权限，需要你在手机上点的时候会停下来告诉你。API Key 由你自己在 Mika 里填，不经过它。 **装好之后：让电脑上的 AI 工具直接用 Mika（MCP）** 手机用数据线连着电脑，在电脑上运行： ``` adb shell sh /sdcard/Android/data/com.wangzan101.mika/files/connect-computer.sh adb forward tcp:8765 tcp:8765 ``` 第一条会打开 Mika 的电脑连接，并打印连接信息（地址 `http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp` 和令牌）；把它们填进电脑上 AI 工具的 MCP 配置，它就能给 Mika 派任务、查进度、拿结果。手机上不用点；只经数据线连接、要令牌，Wi-Fi 上连不到；付款这类确认只能在手机上点。用方式二安装时，AI 助手会顺手帮你接好。详见[电脑连接说明](docs/mcp.md)。 > **English summary** > > Mika is an Android app that takes a one-sentence request and carries it out on your phone. It drives apps on a private background screen (so you can keep using your phone), browses the web in a built-in desktop-class browser, and runs scripts in a local Linux sandbox. You bring your own model API key (several providers are supported as presets, plus any OpenAI-compatible, Anthropic, Gemini or OpenAI Responses endpoint). There is no Mika server: your requests go only to the model provider you configure. > > Status: **public beta**, changing quickly (see [Releases](https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/releases) for versions and changes). Chat, web and sandbox tasks work on Android 11+; phone app control needs Android 12+, with Android 14+ recommended. The sandbox runs on arm64 devices only. The app UI is available in Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese and English (follows your system language; switch in Settings › Language); see the [full English README](README.en.md). Licensed under Apache-2.0. ## Beta 说明 - 这是早期公开测试版，功能和界面还在快速变化，升级时可能有不兼容的改动。 - 目前主要在一台安卓 14 手机上测试过。别的安卓版本、别的手机上可能遇到没见过的问题，欢迎[反馈](#参与贡献)。 - Mika 会替你操作第三方 App 和网站，请先读[免责声明](#免责声明)。 ## 演示

## 能做什么 你用一句话交代一件事，Mika 在手机上替你办。 ### 操作任何 App，不占你的屏幕 手机上装的 App 都能操作，不用事先适配：Mika 像人一样看屏幕、找按钮、点击输入，看得到就能操作。 - 在一块单独的后台屏上打开 App、读界面、点击、输入、滚动，你照常用手机；对话页上的小画面实时显示它在做什么。 - 能逐屏读长列表和聊天记录，比如「帮我总结一下某个群今天都聊了些啥」。 - 界面读不出来的 App（自己画界面、控件没有名字）也能用：Mika 用随 APK 自带的文字识别读屏上的字；配了能看图的模型时，还能看图找按钮和输入框。 - 能把一段文字直接分享进某个 App（发消息、记笔记），收件人和发送仍由 Mika 在那一页上点。 - 系统问「用哪个 App 打开」、装了两份的 App 问「打开哪一个」、一个 App 打开另一个 App（比如跳到付款页）时，Mika 认得出来：能处理的接着做，要你选或要你亲手处理的，会停下来请你在屏幕上操作。 - 需要你亲手处理的事（登录、验证码、付款）会发通知请你接管：App 挪到主屏，你处理完交还，Mika 重新核实再继续。 ### 内置浏览器 - 任何网站都能打开：在后台打开网页，用真实的点击和键盘输入操作页面，默认按电脑版网页打开。 - 能读页面正文，也能读页面自己收到的数据；支持下载、上传。 - 登录过的网站保持登录；侧栏「浏览器」里可以自己浏览，在这里登录的网站 Mika 办事时也能直接用。 - 翻页有节奏：同一个网站连着换页会停一停，对限制浏览快慢的网站停得更久；认得出风控拦截页，交给你处理而不是硬闯。 ### 此刻的屏幕 - 你在别的 App 里时，屏幕边上有一颗 Mika 悬浮胶囊，显示后台任务的进展、要你处理的事和结果，点开可以插话、回答、同意或停止。 - **双击胶囊**，把你正在看的这一屏发给 Mika，比如「这个怎么回」「帮我记下来」；也可以在卡片里截屏、补一句话再发。 ### 定时与条件任务 - 「明早 9 点提醒我」「每天早上看看天气，下雨才告诉我」「每周五做某件事」。 - 到点在原对话里执行，结果送回来；定时任务页可以暂停、改时间、立即执行、删除。 ### 随时插话、随时停 - 任务进行中可以继续说话，补充或更正要求，Mika 在下一步之前读到。 - 按停止后，Mika 会补几行交代：做了什么、看到了什么、发出了几次、哪些没做完。下次说「继续」它知道从哪接着做。 ### 询问 / 自主 - 默认是**询问**：只有花钱（下单、付款）先问你，发消息、提交、删除这些都直接做完。也可以换成**自主**，连付款也不先问。详见[下文](#询问--自主模式)。 ### 记忆 - 记住你明确说过的事实、偏好和做事方式（做事方式要你批准），可以查看、修改、删除；只从你自己说的话里记，密码、验证码、卡号这类不记。记忆加密保存在手机上。 ### 熟悉的 App 和网站，做得更快更稳 没有任何说明，Mika 也能看着屏幕把事办成。有些 App 和网站另外写了使用知识（入口在哪、常见做法、要注意什么），Mika 用到时自动查阅，少走弯路。比如进了聊天 App 直接知道怎么找联系人、翻聊天记录；打开招聘网站知道怎么筛岗位、打招呼。另有几类事情的通用做法。知识持续增加，人人可以补充：它们是放在 [`core/src/main/resources/knowledge/`](core/src/main/resources/knowledge/) 和 [`core/src/main/resources/skills/`](core/src/main/resources/skills/) 下的纯文本文件，[欢迎补充](#参与贡献)。 已经写了使用知识的（没写到的 App 和网站照样能用）： | 类别 | 内置 | |---|---| | **App** | Android 设置、百家号、哔哩哔哩、BOSS直聘、Chrome、得到、抖音、飞书、Gmail、即刻、快手、领英、QQ邮箱、Telegram、今日头条、Uber、Uber Eats、微信、微博、WhatsApp、闲鱼、小红书、知乎 | | **网站** | Amazon、哔哩哔哩、Google Calendar、豆瓣、抖音、Instagram、Gmail、Google Maps、Telegram、百度贴吧、微博、搜狗微信、WhatsApp、小红书、小宇宙、YouTube、知乎、BOSS直聘 | | **通用做法**（技能） | 把内容整理成文字、处理 PDF 文档、查清一件事、消息与邮件 | ### 成批的事 - 成批做事（比如逐个打招呼、投递）直接开始，不用先跟你确认名单；每两次之间隔开一段随机时间，做到网站自己说「到上限了」就停下告诉你。 ### 过程可查 - 回答下面列出来源（读过的页面、截图）；每次任务都有可回看的过程记录。 - 每次任务一行小结：总用时、和模型来回几次、用了多少 Token、多久看到第一次反馈；设置里的「Token 用量」按天、按服务商、按模型统计。 ### Linux 沙箱 - 每个对话一个工作区，可以跑 Python、Node 和 shell 命令，处理你发来的文件，把结果存到手机的「下载/Mika」。 - 默认断网，需要时在设置里的「文件与计算环境」打开「允许脚本联网」。只支持 arm64 设备。 ### 电脑上的 AI 工具也能用（CLI / MCP） 手机连着电脑时，电脑上的 AI 工具可以通过 MCP 把任务交给 Mika，在手机上办完把结果拿回去。一条命令打开，只经数据线、要令牌；也可以在设置里打开局域网连接（默认关）。见[电脑连接说明](docs/mcp.md)。 也可以安装[电脑端 CLI 与 Agent Skill](docs/cli.md),用 `mika connect`、`mika task run`、`mika task wait` 完成连接和任务交接。CLI 与 MCP 并列接入同一份手机任务服务,CLI 不需要配置 MCP;需要包含任务 API v1 的 APK。 ## 快速开始 ### 系统要求 | 项目 | 要求 | |---|---| | 安装、聊天、网页与沙箱任务 | 安卓 11 及以上（沙箱仅支持 arm64） | | 操作手机 App | 安卓 12 及以上；安卓 12、13 上后台操作可能影响主屏焦点 | | 推荐 | 安卓 14 及以上：后台屏有自己的焦点，不影响你在主屏打字；不同对话的任务同时进行也需要它 | | Linux 沙箱 | 仅 arm64 设备；其他设备照常安装，沙箱显示「此设备不支持」 | | 模型 | 一个支持工具调用的大模型 API Key | ### 1. 下载安装 从 [Releases](https://github.com/wangzan101/Mika/releases/latest) 下载最新的 APK 安装。 ### 2. 无障碍（可以先跳过） Mika 靠无障碍读界面、做点按。不用手动去开：下一步配对成功后，Mika 会自己把它打开。从 GitHub 下载安装的 App，手动打开无障碍时常被系统拦下（提示「受限制的设置」），让 Mika 自己开能省掉这个麻烦。向导里到这一步时选「跳过」即可。 ### 3. 配对无线调试（只需一次） 打开设置里的「设置手机操作」向导，照着清单做：打开开发者选项、USB 调试、无线调试，然后用 6 位配对码配对。开发者选项里 Mika 没提到的开关不要动，有的会清除手机数据，比如「以 16KB 页面大小启动设备」。 第一次设置、卡在某一步，或者不知道配对码填在哪里：看[手机操作设置指南](docs/setup-guide.md)，每一步都写了在哪里点、怎么算成功、常见问题怎么办。 为什么要这一步：Mika 有一个内置的手机助手，要在后台屏上启动和操作 App，需要借用安卓自带的无线调试来启动它。全程在手机上完成，不需要电脑和数据线。配对过后，如果无线调试被系统关掉了（换 Wi-Fi、重启手机后安卓会关掉它），Mika 在你允许的前提下会自己把它重新打开。 手边有电脑和数据线的话，也可以不配对：先打开一次 Mika，插着线在电脑上运行 `adb shell sh /sdcard/Android/data/com.wangzan101.mika/files/usb-start.sh` 启动手机助手；但每次重启手机后都要再运行一次。这些也可以交给电脑上的 AI 助手，见[用电脑上的 AI 助手安装](docs/install-with-agent.md)。 只用上网、文件和聊天的话，这一步可以先跳过。 ### 4. 添加模型 打开设置里的「模型」（第一次打开 App 时也会引导你）。 内置 DeepSeek、通义千问、Kimi、智谱、硅基流动、火山方舟、MiniMax、阶跃星辰、腾讯混元、百度千帆、OpenRouter、OpenCode Go、Anthropic、Gemini、OpenAI、xAI、Mistral、Groq、Ollama、LM Studio 等服务商预设；其他服务商选「自定义」，OpenAI 兼容、Anthropic、Gemini、OpenAI Responses 接口都能接。 也可以不填 Key，用账号登录：添加服务商最上面是「用账号登录 · 不用填 Key」一组，点一家先看说明，再去浏览器里登录，登录后回到 Mika，能看到账号、可用的模型，可以直接设为主模型。 - **ChatGPT**（Plus 或 Pro，用你的套餐额度）：点「使用 ChatGPT 继续」，在浏览器里登录。 - **xAI / Grok**（SuperGrok 或 X Premium+ 订阅）：浏览器里打开 xAI 的确认页，核对手机上显示的短码后同意。这项登录借用 xAI 官方命令行工具的公开登录入口，不是 xAI 专门给 Mika 开的，xAI 可能限制这种用法；有的订阅档位登录后仍不能调用（提示 403），那时改用 xAI 的 API Key。 - **OpenRouter**：OpenRouter 官方给第三方应用的授权。同意后 OpenRouter 给 Mika 一把属于你的 Key（名字是 Mika），用量从你的 OpenRouter 余额里扣；不想用了，在 OpenRouter 的 Keys 页面删掉它。 退出登录只清这台手机上的登录信息。 1. 添加服务商：选一个预设，或选「自定义」填接口地址；填 API Key。Ollama、LM Studio 这类自己机器上跑的服务，地址预填了默认端口，改成那台机器的地址即可，Key 可不填。 2. 点「测试并保存」，连上第一家时会自动选一个主模型。 3. 主模型要支持工具调用。可选：看图模型（看懂界面、看图找按钮）、轻量模型（便宜快的即可，处理判断结局、提取记忆等小事）。 用 ChatGPT 登录或 Responses 接口的模型，可在各用途卡片下调整「思考强度」。默认用服务商默认值；选「用主模型」时也跟随它的强度，明确选同一个模型则可分别设置。档位优先采用服务商报告的列表；没报告时提供手动选项，实际支持情况以服务端为准。更高强度通常更慢、消耗更多 token。 ### 5. 试一试 空对话里有几条示例，点一下就能改了再发。也可以这样说： - 「帮我总结一下微信群今天都聊了些啥」 - 「打开小红书，帮我总结一下某个博主最近发的内容」 - 「帮我订明天早上 9:40、9:50、10:00 的闹钟」 - 「每天早上 8 点看看天气，下雨才告诉我」 ## 询问 / 自主模式 全局一个开关：设置里的「开发者选项」→「自主模式」，关着是询问，打开是自主。 | 模式 | 行为 | |---|---| | **询问**（默认） | 只有花钱的那一步先问你：下单、提交订单，或者页面上显示着应付金额时的确认、提交。卡片上写明在哪、买什么、多少钱，只能同意这一次或不同意。付款本身由你亲手完成。发消息、发帖、提交表单、删除、改设置这些都不问，直接做完。 | | **自主** | 连付款也不先问你，直接做完。成批做事时两次之间的间隔照样保留。 | - 换了开关管之后的所有任务；正在做的任务从询问换成自主，下一步起付款也不再问。 - 登录、验证码、付款密码这类要你亲手处理的事，两种模式都会请你接管；信息不够、或者只有你能选（比如两个同名联系人选哪个）时，也会问你。 - 定时任务等你不在场的任务，在询问模式下遇到要花钱的一步不会等人，会直接不做，并照实告诉你哪一步没做成；别的照常做完。 ## 数据与隐私 - **没有 Mika 的服务器。** 你的话、屏幕内容、截图只发给你自己配置的模型服务商。 - API Key、记忆和用户画像用安卓密钥库加密，保存在手机上。对话、运行记录、Token 用量都只存在本机。 - 检查更新只访问 GitHub。 - 内置浏览器访问的是你让它去的网站；沙箱默认断网。 ## 免责声明 - 用自动化方式操作第三方 App 和网站，可能违反它们的用户协议，有被限制功能、封号的风险。请自行判断、自担风险。 - 你同意的动作（以及自主模式下 Mika 替你做的动作）由你负责。重要的事请用询问模式，并检查结果。 - 仓库有两个模块：`:core` 是纯 Kotlin，主循环、工具、提示词、知识都在这里，可以在电脑上用单测和假模型跑；`:app` 是安卓宿主。 - 沙箱的原生程序和自带运行环境已在仓库里；重新构建见 [`tools/sandbox/README.md`](tools/sandbox/README.md)。 - 真机评测见 [`eval/README.md`](eval/README.md)。 ### 模型配置细节 - 三个用途：**主模型**（办事，要支持工具调用）、**看图模型**（描述界面、看图定位；新装默认不用，可选「用主模型」）、**轻量模型**（判断结局、提取记忆、理解意图等小事，默认用主模型）。 - 「测试并保存」先调一次服务商公开的列模型接口，再带一个试用的工具，请会当主模型的那个模型调用它（用掉几十个 token）；都成了才保存，哪一步不成当场说原因（服务端的报错原样显示）。先试哪个：这家自己的模型在前（例如通义千问先试名字里有 qwen 的），再是列表明说能调用工具的，向量、重排、语音、画图这类不试。试的模型是它自己的问题（这个账号没开通或没权限、没有这个模型、不会调用工具）时接着试下一个，至多 3 个：通过的当主模型，并说一句先试的哪个没通过；都没通过也保存服务商（Key 是对的），不定主模型，说明原因、请你从列表里选一个开通了的，选的时候先试调用。Key、网络、地址不对照旧不保存。没列出模型时（可能这家不提供列表，也可能地址或接口类型填错了），先填一个模型名，再测试就用它试调用，通了才保存；找不到这个模型时说清是哪个、模型名大概长什么样。自定义填的是某家的官方地址时，提醒改用那家的预设（一点就换，Key 留着）。不提供列表的服务商，在选用途时手填的模型名同样先试调用；以前没试过的，服务商那一行提醒「没测试通过」，点进去可以「重新测试」。 - 模型列表上的能力标签（工具调用、看图、上下文长度）：接口给了的照实显示，没给的沿用预设初值并标「未确认」，只作参考，不拦。 - 「看图定位已验证」在设置里的「开发者选项」（调试版可见），对当前看图模型生效。 ### 文档 - [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md)：整体结构。 - [`docs/roadmap.md`](docs/roadmap.md)：已完成、接下来、已知问题与暂缓。 -
